info.disambiguation: American singer, guitarist, songwriter and music producer
info.bio:
Bo Diddley (McComb, 30 de diciembre de 1928 - 2 de junio de 2008), es un compositor, cantante y guitarrista americano que ha tenido una gran influencia en el rock and roll. Se le suele considerar como la figura predominante en la transición del blues al rock and roll, creador de ritmos básicos con un sonido duro y afilado de su guitarra. Por ello tiene el sobre nombre de "The Originator" (El Autor).

Su música

Si en el rock and roll Elvis Presley es el rey y Chuck Berry su poeta, Bo Diddley es su arquitecto.

scenes.name: Rhythm and blues
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: En los cuarenta, los combos de jump como el Tympany Five de Louis Jordan sustituyeron a las big bands: baile, ritmo, scat, solo de saxo. Gente que trabajaba duro todo el día necesitaba música fuerte y con alma: un grito sincero, un saxo, una guitarra rockera. Su «misma vulgaridad», dice LeRoi Jones, aseguraba su conexión con la vida de la gente, y esa vulgaridad fue el ingrediente principal del funk. Despreciado por los intelectuales como mal jazz, el R&B dio a Chuck Berry, Little Richard y Bo Diddley, inspiró el rock and roll y la invasión británica, y en el chitlin circuit fue el útero del funk. Con Live at the Apollo de James Brown (1962, disco de oro) el R&B se hizo mayor; de él salieron Ray Charles, Brown y Aretha Franklin.

scenes.name: Rock'n'roll
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Fusión de rhythm'n'blues y country, con mucho más peso del primero. Chuck Berry inventa en 1955 el rock'n'roll tal como se conocerá durante cincuenta años (la guitarra como instrumento protagonista, canciones propias que hablan a los adolescentes); Bo Diddley aporta el ritmo «hambone», Little Richard y Esquerita el histerismo y el maquillaje (el primer «decadence-rock»), Jerry Lee Lewis el piano feroz y Sun Records el rockabilly. Elvis Presley es, para Scaruffi, «la primera gran estafa del rock'n'roll». Buddy Holly y Eddie Cochran abren otra vía; en paralelo nacen el soul (Ray Charles), la exótica (Martin Denny, Esquivel), la música electrónica de cinta y, en Gran Bretaña, el skiffle.

mentions.author: Piero Scaruffi
mentions.text: …and blacks did not get the same airplay as white musicians. He remained a cult item. In the same city and in the same year, another black musician, Bo Diddley, invented the "hambone" rhythm (a syncopated boogie rhythm), that harked back to tribal Africa and gave songs such as Bo Diddley (1955) and Who Do You Love (1955) a suspenseful, sinister and hypnotic quality. Rock'n'roll was certainly more closely related to rhythm'n'blues than to country music. Chicago rhythm'n'blues naturally morphed into rock'n'roll with black musicians such as Chuck Berry and Bo Diddley. podcast.title: Explosion into Public Consciousness (1955)
podcast.body: Bo Diddly, along with Elvis, Chuck Berry, Little Richard, and Bill Haley, exploded into public consciousness in 1955, marking the birth of rock and roll. "they all exploded into public consciousness that year, 1955, the birth of rock and roll."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Performer at Madison Square Garden (1971)
podcast.body: Bo Diddley was among the "classic rock and rollers" on the bill at the nostalgic multi-act concert at New York's Madison Square Garden in the fall of 1971, where Rick Nelson experienced a poor audience reception. "Among the classic rock and rollers on the bill were Chuck Berry, Bo Didley and Bobby Ridell."

podcast.body: Bo Diddley was one of the "living legends long past their prime" inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1987, contrasting with Aretha Franklin, who was a current hitmaker. "to living legends long past their prime like Bo Didley."

podcast.title: Bo Diddley Beat
podcast.body: The "Bo Diddley beat" is cited as an example of a rhythm and beat that is "not protected" by copyright, illustrating that specific rhythmic patterns can be used by multiple artists without legal consequence. "That's why you can have bow diddly. And Iggy Pop. And you too. And Jet."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Co-Writer of "Love Is Strange"
podcast.body: Bo Diddley co-wrote "Love Is Strange," a song that was a favorite of Buddy Holly's and served as the musical basis for Holly's first solo single, "Words of Love." "who had co-written Love Is Strange as a cricket side."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty-One: "That'll Be the Day", by the Crickets

podcast.title: Co-writer of "Love Is Strange"
podcast.body: Bo Diddley is credited as a co-writer for "Love Is Strange," claiming to have written the lyrics (credited to his wife Ethel Smith), while Jody Williams wrote the music. "Now, Deadly claimed that what he told the song's publishers was that Jody Williams wrote the music while he wrote the lyrics, but he asked that the credit for the lyrics bepotting the name of his wife, Ethel Smith."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 49: "Love is Strange" by Mickey and Sylvia

podcast.title: Dispute over Writing Credits for "Love Is Strange"
podcast.body: Jody Williams, who played lead guitar on Diddley's unreleased version of "Love Is Strange," was not credited for the music and blamed Diddley. Diddley argued that most people he signed contracts with were "liars and thieves" and he wasn't surprised Williams's name was omitted, leading to a decades-long estrangement between them. "Williams as Deadly didn't, and Williams blamed Deadly for the emission while Deadly just said with some evidence that most of the people he signed contracts with were liars and thieves, and that it didn't surprise him that they'd missed Williams's name off."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 49: "Love is Strange" by Mickey and Sylvia

podcast.title: Divorce and Destroyed Papers
podcast.body: Before his divorce from Ethel Smith, she reportedly burned all his papers, which Diddley claimed was to prevent him from proving he had given her money, making it impossible to ascertain the exact terms of his contracts, including those related to "Love Is Strange." "We'll never know for sure what was actually in Deadly's contract, because, again, according to Deadly, just before he and Smith divorced, she burned all his papers, so she could claim that he never gave her any money, and he couldn't prove otherwise."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 49: "Love is Strange" by Mickey and Sylvia

podcast.title: Giant of Rock Music
podcast.body: Bo Diddley is recognized as one of the significant figures in the broader landscape of rock music. "Where would we be with a bow diddly and little Richard and Jimmy Hendrix?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on The Crickets' Music
podcast.body: The Crickets recorded the song "Not Fade Away," which they described as being "patented after Bo Didley," indicating a direct influence from his distinctive musical style. "they went into the studio and caught another song they had patented after Bo Didley, who had co-written Love Is Strange as a cricket side."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty-One: "That'll Be the Day", by the Crickets

podcast.title: Influenced by Gene Autry
podcast.body: Bo Diddley was one of the artists whose musical development was shaped by the influence of Gene Autry, a leading Western music star during the late 1930s and early 1940s. "influenced everyone from Les Paul to Bowie Didley."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Popularizer of the "Bo Diddley Beat"
podcast.body: Bo Diddley is renowned for using a particular rhythm so effectively that it became known as the "Bo Diddley beat." Although the beat itself originated at least 50 years before his time, he was instrumental in introducing it to rock and roll, influencing numerous artists from Iggy Pop to Joan Jett. "Bow didn't invent that beat. It's history goes back at least 50 years, but he was the one who introduced it to rock and roll."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sale of "Love Is Strange" Share
podcast.body: According to Bo Diddley, he later sold his share in the song "Love Is Strange" to Sylvia (Van Topoele/Robinson) sometime in the early 1960s, a decision that proved astute given Sylvia's subsequent business acumen. "According to Deadly, he also later sold his own share in the song to Sylvia, sometime in the early 60s."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 49: "Love is Strange" by Mickey and Sylvia

podcast.title: Session Guitarist for Other Artists
podcast.body: Diddley was friendly with Mickey Baker and used Baker as a session guitarist on outside recordings he produced for other artists, including Billy Stewart and The Marquees (which featured Marvin Gaye). "At the time, Deadly was friendly with Mickey Baker and was using Baker as a session guitarist on outside recordings he was producing for other artists, including recordings with Billy Stuart and with the marquees, a vocal group which featured a young singer named Marvin Gaye."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

xref.title: "Lady Bo" Nickname and Relationship with Bo Diddley
xref.body: Peggy Jones earned the nickname "Lady Bo" due to her close musical partnership with Bo Diddley, which led many to mistakenly assume they were a couple. In reality, she was married to the band's bass player. "Peggy was also known as Lady Bo because she and Bo were so tight that everybody just assumed that they were a couple. Not true. She was actually married to the band's bass player."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Departure for The Jewels
xref.body: Peggy Jones contributed to many Bo Diddley records until approximately 1961, when she left the band to dedicate her time to her own group, The Jewels. "Peggy ended up on a lot of Bo Didley records until about 1961 before she left a spend time with her own band called The Jewels."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: One of the First Female Rock Guitarists
xref.body: Peggy Jones joined Bo Diddley's band as a guitarist in 1957 and is recognized as one of the first female rock guitarists in a famous rock band. She later became known for her experimental use of guitar synthesizers, a rare application in R&B music at the time. "This Black woman was recognized as one of the first female rock guitarists in a famous rock band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Opening Acts
xref.body: He opened for various prominent artists and bands, including The Byrds, Iron Butterfly, and Bo Diddley. "He landed opening gaze with everyone from the birds to iron butterfly to bow didly"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Pioneering Female Electric Guitarist in Rock
xref.body: Peggy Jones, also known as Lady Bo, joined Bo Diddley's band in 1957 as a rhythm guitarist, potentially making her the first woman to be visibly playing electric guitar in a rock band. Her recruitment came after Diddley observed her carrying a guitar case. "And as such, she might have very well been the first woman to be visible as an electric guitarist in a rock band. This was 1957."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Use of Bo Diddley Beat
xref.body: Iggy Pop is mentioned as an artist who uses rhythms and beats that are not protected by copyright, specifically implying the use of the "Bo Diddley beat." "That's why you can have bow diddly. And Iggy Pop. And you too. And Jet."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
